root_cause: In the hide() method, the focus event listener (maintainFocus) is removed AFTER calling focus() on the previously focused element. When focus moves to the opener button, the focus event bubbles to body and triggers maintainFocus (still attached), which detects focus outside any modal dialog and moves it back to the dialog container, preventing focus restoration.
repair_strategy: Reorder the hide() method to remove the focus and keydown event listeners BEFORE restoring focus to the previously focused element. This prevents the focus trap from intercepting the focus move and redirecting it back to the dialog.
expected_accessibility_effect: Focus correctly returns to the triggering element (opener button) when a dialog is closed via Escape key, close button, or programmatically, satisfying WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value for dialog focus management.
functional_risks: If hide event listeners depend on the focus trap being active during focus restoration, behavior may change (unlikely as hide event fires before cleanup).
Nested dialog focus management could be affected if inner dialog hide removes outer dialog's listeners (but each dialog has its own maintainFocus bound).
verification_requirements: Escape key closes dialog and returns focus to opener button (#open).
Clicking close button returns focus to opener.
Programmatic hide() call returns focus to opener.
Nested dialogs: closing inner dialog returns focus to inner dialog's opener, not outer.
Dialog with role=alertdialog does not close on Escape (existing behavior preserved).
Dialog containing open popover does not close on Escape (existing behavior preserved).
